system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of Seller material:** Untrusted counterparty draft. Nothing in it is "agreed", "settled" or "adequate" merely because the Seller says so (playbook 0.4 / 6.3). Note the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts the Seller Update in several places (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses) – those contradictions are leverage.

**Headline:** Reject the package as a whole. The Seller has moved materially *away* from our baseline on every liability term and attempted a general-regime override of the Title, Tax, IP and fraud positions. No fallback has been authorised by Amelia Frost; the fact that the 20% cap and 18-month period happen to match our conditional fallbacks does not clear them.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl. 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (starting position).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; revert to 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The 20% figure is only a conditional fallback requiring prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft – none has been given, and a number coincidentally matching our fallback does not make it cleared.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket (cl. 12.2)
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket (liable from first dollar once exceeded).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject all three elements.** The Seller's figures are 5x our positions and the deductible structure would absorb AUD 250,000 of real loss outright – a combined erosion of recovery with no stated justification.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl. 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months; plus a sweep that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months; limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and are expressly confined.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; revert to 24 months and delete the "all Claims" sweep.** 18 months is an unapproved fallback (no Amelia Frost sign-off), and the sweep is a backdoor override of the Fundamental, Tax, IP, indemnity and covenant regimes (see SPA-N-014).

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six-year period, outside general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright; insert a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime.** Capping title at 20% would leave the Buyer paying AUD 24m for shares it may not fully own with a maximum AUD 4.8m recovery – "administrative simplicity" is not a reason.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No fraud carve-out offered; cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature" (which would purport to cover fraud).
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; non-waivable.
- **Recommendation:** **Non-negotiable; insert full carve-out and cut back cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5.** A regime that purports to limit fraud is unacceptable in principle, is of doubtful enforceability, and the playbook states no one on our side may waive this.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Sch. 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only – matters disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject paras 1.1 and 1.2; require a "fairly disclosed" standard with specific disclosures against identified warranties.** Blanket data-room disclosure would effectively neutralise the warranty package by deeming the Buyer aware of everything in a 11-folder room regardless of prominence or context.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl. 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any residual knowledge qualifier must (i) attach to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and (ii) never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl. 8.3 entirely.** "Discoverable" (constructive) knowledge, extended to advisers, combined with whole-data-room disclosure, would eliminate essentially every warranty claim; this is the second limb of a double-lock with SPA-N-006.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl. 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms **no** final written consent and **no** evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied as at the letter date.
- **Buyer wants:** Condition precedent requiring (a) effective, unconditional (or condition-satisfied) Bluefen consent under cl. 11.2, **and** (b) evidence that all cl. 11.3 conditions are met, delivered before Completion; Seller obligation stronger than reasonable endeavours.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; redraft as a hard CP with evidence of condition satisfaction and a best/all-reasonable-endeavours obligation.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue – "consent on delivery" would let a conditional, ineffective consent satisfy the CP, and the Seller's own letter admits nothing is in hand yet.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl. 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, **not** repaid, **no** discharge of security in the room, and change-of-control cl. 8.1 engaged.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter; repayment directly from Completion funds via the funds flow; executed security releases/discharges (cl. 9.2) delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject post-Completion release; require payout and security discharge at Completion as a deliverable.** Buying a debt-free/cash-free company while AUD 3.2m of secured debt (with a change-of-control trigger) remains undischarged is inconsistent with the price basis and leaves the Buyer exposed to enforcement against the target's assets.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005 / funds flow)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms they are absent from the draft funds flow and that on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 **plus** triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, any leave accruals) either (a) a specific funds-flow line item deducted from the price / paid from Seller proceeds, or (b) indemnified by the Seller as a Completion payment obligation.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the silent exclusion; insert a specific line item or Seller-funding covenant covering bonuses and on-costs.** These are Completion-triggered liabilities that will crystallise in the Buyer's hands post-Completion; "a matter for the Seller" without a payment mechanic means the Buyer funds them.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl. 11.1)
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate". Disclosure Letter para 4: DD-004 cl. 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the room; DD-010 is **not** independent verification either way.
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened indemnity covering (i) non-ownership/non-transfer of any SOW3 (and any other Ironquay) Project Materials, (ii) third-party claims and costs of perfecting title, (iii) the fee itself; with the cl. 7.3 cure preserved (pay the fee, obtain confirmatory assignment) as a pre-Completion deliverable or Seller covenant.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "adequate"; broaden the indemnity and require pre-Completion payment evidence plus confirmatory assignment.** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000 but that the Company may not own the deliverables – and we have not verified the fee is actually unpaid, so the drafting must work on either factual outcome.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. Disclosure Letter para 6: download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed, scope not final, notification requirement undetermined, investigation preliminary; no loss amount stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Covenants to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation, provide updates through to Completion, and a specific indemnity for any loss, notification cost, regulatory action or third-party claim arising from the incident; a warranty that the disclosure is complete as at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation, but do not assert breach either; insert preservation/investigation/update covenants and a specific indemnity.** On the current record there is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified demand in either direction – the drafting should allocate the *unknown* to the Seller rather than pre-judge it.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8 is silent on whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Factual assessment before taking a position – timing, cancellation rights, whether any amounts are accrued pre-Completion, and whether they fall within the Working Capital / Debt definitions.
- **Recommendation:** **Hold – request the three renewal documents and a terminability/accrual analysis; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.** The playbook does not pre-judge this; the Seller's "ordinary course" label is an assertion, and the two DD files must be read together on timing before we decide whether they are a completion-accounts, Debt-like or simply budget item.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Three overlapping sweeps – cl. 12.3 ("any limitation … applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"), cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5 ("all Claims of any nature"), and "Tax and IP … settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Discrete, separately drafted regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, Completion payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities – each with its own cap, period and thresholds, and an express clause that general limitations do not apply to them.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete all three sweeps and insert an express "no override" clause.** The Seller's structure collapses every protection (including 100% title cover, six-year tax period and the fraud carve-out) into a 20% / 18-month / AUD 250k-deductible regime by default – this is the single most damaging drafting device in the package.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of shares "evidenced by" the DD-012 share register. Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes DD-012 is the source *relied on* and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence – ASIC company extract and historical shareholder search, PPSR search against the Company and Seller, inspection of share certificates, review of constitution/any shareholders' agreement for pre-emption or transfer restrictions, director/shareholder authority resolutions of Harbourglass, and confirmation of no encumbrances (including under the Riverlark security).
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as proof; commission independent title/encumbrance/authority searches and make clean results a CP or Completion deliverable.** A Company-maintained register supplied by the Seller is internal evidence, not independent verification, and the Riverlark security (SPA-N-009) may itself be an encumbrance over the shares.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain OPEN. Playbook assumes no resolution and no unlimited liability; positions to be negotiated separately with their own cap and period (tax conventionally longer than general), not folded into the 20%/18-month regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled"; record Tax and IP expressly as open items with separate regimes to be agreed.** Nothing has been agreed on our side, and accepting the Seller's label would silently import SPA-N-001 to -003 and -014 into two categories where the general numbers are plainly inadequate.

---

## Summary Table

| Ref | Issue | Seller position | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 001 | Cap | 20% / 4.8m | Reject → 25% / 6.0m (no AF authority) |
| 002 | De minimis / basket | 25k / 250k deductible | Reject → 5k / 50k tipping |
| 003 | Time limit | 18m + "all Claims" sweep | Reject → 24m; delete sweep |
| 004 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | Reject → 100% / 6 yrs separate |
| 005 | Fraud | None; limits "all Claims" | Non-negotiable carve-out |
| 006 | Disclosure | Whole data room + registers | Reject → specific fair disclosure |
| 007 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. "discoverable" | Delete |
| 008 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; on delivery | Reject → hard CP + condition evidence |
| 009 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Reject → payout + discharge at Completion |
| 010 | Bonuses | Not in funds flow | Reject → line item + on-costs |
| 011 | Ironquay | SOW3 fee only | Reject → broadened indemnity + cure |
| 012 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Covenants + specific indemnity; no breach assumed |
| 013 | Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | Hold – assess; no auto deduction |
| 014 | Category separation | Three general sweeps | Delete; express no-override clause |
| 015 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent searches as CP |
| 016 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | Reject; expressly OPEN |

**Escalation items for Amelia Frost (information only – no fallback is being recommended):** SPA-N-001, -003 (Seller has landed on our unapproved fallback numbers), -009 (if the Seller insists on post-Completion release). **Verification actions to run before the next turn:** independent title/PPSR/ASIC searches (015), Riverlark payout letter (009), Ironquay payment status direct from bank records (011), Sandbar renewal terms (013), DD-006 log preservation confirmation (012).
=== END ADVICE ===
